questions.q: Which table defines a catalog variable itself (its label, type, and conditions), as opposed to a requester's specific answer?
options: sc_item_option
item_option_new
sc_cat_item
io_set_item
questions.explain: item_option_new is the variable's definition, built once by the administrator. sc_item_option captures the actual value a requester submits.

questions.q: Why is a Reference variable generally better than a Single Line Text variable for a field like "Requested for"?
options: Reference variables render faster on the request form
Single Line Text variables are not permitted on catalog items
A Reference variable points to an actual record on another table, so the answer is always a valid, resolvable record rather than free-typed text
There is no real difference between the two types
questions.explain: A Reference variable guarantees the captured value is a real record workflows and approvals can act on, unlike free text that could contain a typo or an unmatched name.

questions.q: What does a Variable Set (io_set_item) solve that defining the same variables on every catalog item does not?
options: It removes the need for any variable types other than Choice
It groups variables once so a change propagates to every catalog item using that set, instead of needing to be fixed on each item separately
It is required before a catalog item can have a Price field
It converts all variables into Reference type automatically
questions.explain: A Variable Set is reusable — update a variable inside the set once, and every catalog item attached to that set picks up the change.

questions.q: What distinguishes a multi-row variable set from a standard (one-to-one) variable set?
options: A multi-row set lets the requester add multiple repeated rows of the same group of variables on one form
A multi-row set can only contain Checkbox variables
A multi-row set cannot be reused across more than one catalog item
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: Multi-row variable sets are used when a requester needs to submit several repeats of the same fields, such as one row per additional attendee.

questions.q: Per the practical test given in this lesson, when should a variable be placed directly on a single catalog item rather than inside a shared Variable Set?
options: Always — variables should never be grouped into sets
Only when the variable type is Multiple Choice
Whenever the variable is genuinely unique to that one item, rather than logically identical to a variable needed on other items
Only on Record Producers
questions.explain: A variable unique to one item (like a specific room number) belongs on that item directly; one needed identically across multiple items belongs in a shared set.
